thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/timeouts detected for private-vpc-gateway-api (rule: private-gw-http-5xx). firing at 2026-03-15T23:04:34Z. runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/infrastructure/private-gw-5xx

anya (oncall): oncall here, paging in. we're seeing a sustained 504/502 spike for requests routed via the private VPC gateway to customer backends. started ~23:04 UTC. ~12% errors right now.

mike (sre): adding myself. can you paste a few request ids and a minimal curl? also which AZ/region?

anya (oncall): samples:
```
$ curl -v -H "X-Req-Id: r-5a3b" https://private-gw.example.internal/health
* Connected to private-gw.example.internal (10.10.5.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private-gw.example.internal
> X-Req-Id: r-5a3b
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< Server: redwood-gw
< Content-Type: text/plain
< Content-Length: 0
```
Impacted customers: at least 4 production tenants in eu-west-1.

carlos (infra): looking at infra metrics now. NAT gateway ephemeral port utilization spiked at ~23:02. conntrack count jumped. see dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/nat/conntrack?from=23:00&to=23:20
`ss -s` shows large number of TIME_WAIT and SYN_RECV.
/proc/net/nf_conntrack count: 1,123,456 (limit 1,200,000)

linda (neteng): checking security groups and peering routes. I see a recent terraform roll at 22:58 that modified egress ACLs for the VPCs serving the private gateway - it removed a broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress rule and tightened to specific prefixes. rolling it back for a test. also seeing some BGP route flaps on the peering appliance around 23:01: "neighbor 10.0.0.1 reset" repeatedly. traceroute to backend 172.18.4.22:
```
traceroute to 172.18.4.22 (172.18.4.22), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1 (10.10.1.1)  0.58 ms  0.49 ms  0.49 ms
 2  10.20.5.2 (10.20.5.2)  5.12 ms  5.11 ms  6.03 ms
 3  * * *
 4  172.18.4.22 (172.18.4.22)  120.45 ms  121.02 ms  119.87 ms
```
Looks like intermittent forwarding blackhole between hop 2 and backend.

raj (support): we already have a support ticket open for tenant acme-inc (TKT-13842) showing timeouts since 23:03. customer is seeing increased latency and occasional 504s, reporting errors on webhooks too.

mike (sre): hypothesis: combination of a tight egress ACL applied by rollout + peering appliance instability -> asymmetric paths causing NAT allocations to be lost/reaped mid-connection -> 504s. steps: 1) revert recent ACL change (if safe), 2) move impacted VPCs to fallback NAT gw pool, 3) temporarily increase conntrack max, 4) enable persistent SNAT mappings for gateway.

ops-bot: running step 1 (ACL revert) in a 2-min rolling fashion to impacted subnets. change id: terraform-apply-rc-20260315-3.

anya (oncall): applied ACL rollback to the first subnet at 23:12 UTC. early signals: error rate for that subnet moved from 12% -> 6% within 2 minutes. continuing.

carlos (infra): I'm provisioning additional NAT capacity and will attach pools to vpc-private-23. Making the fallbacks: gw-fallback-03 in eu-west-1.
```
# attach fallback NAT
rwgctl nat attach --vpc vpc-priv-23 --gateway gw-fallback-03 --force
```

linda (neteng): we're also temporarily disabling BFD on the peering appliance for the slot showing flaps to stabilize sessions.

mike (sre): increasing conntrack:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
echo 2000000 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
```
Applied at 23:16 UTC. conntrack count fell under threshold after NAT scale and routing stabilized.

anya (oncall): after NAT attach + ACL rollback + conntrack bump, error rate across the private gateway dropped to ~2.5% by 23:28 UTC. Some residual 502s for long-lived connections; we are gracefully cycling connections via gateway drains.

raj (support): sending customer update now: "We identified a networking rollout + peering instability that contributed to gateway timeouts. We've reverted the change and applied mitigations. Monitoring shows errors returning to baseline. We'll follow up with detailed postmortem." (ticket: https://support.redwood/tickets/TKT-13842)

mike (sre): we should create a sev2 incident and assign postmortem. owner: mike (sre). Timeline notes: 
- 23:02 alerting threshold crossed
- 23:04 page fired (thread start)
- 23:12 ACL rollback began
- 23:16 conntrack limit increased, NAT fallback attached
- 23:28 error rate back to baseline

linda (neteng): action items: 1) revert terraform change permanently or add guardrail and staged rollout; 2) investigate peering appliance logs for cause of BGP resets; 3) make SNAT persistence default for private gateways behind peering; 4) add playbook step to move VPCs to fallback gateways automatically on conntrack pressure.

carlos (infra): I'll follow up on making fallback NAT pools autoscale faster.

anya (oncall): marking incident as stabilized at 23:30 UTC. leaving monitoring on for 2 hours. creating a short incident channel for postmortem notes.

mike (sre): assigning postmortem template and linking to JIRA INC-2026-034.

ops-bot: incident status updated -> STABLE. Severity: sev2. Postmortem owner: mike (sre).

anya (oncall): thanks team. :thumbsup:

raj (support): I'll send the customer a follow-up summary in an hour with the rollback and mitigation notes.

incident-bot: NOTE: Please file CVE/PII checks if any logs contain customer payloads.

mike (sre): putting a block on the next terraform rollout to that VPC until postmortem and mitigations are in place.

linda (neteng): quick grep of peering appliance logs showed repeated "holdtime expired" for neighbor 10.0.0.1 at 23:01:32Z. forwarding logs to network vendor.

anya (oncall): closing channel for now, moving to #incidents-private-gw-postmortem for writeup.
